claim: Rab5 is predominantly monoubiquitinated when FLAG-Rab5 was overexpressed with HA-ubiquitin in HEK 293T cells.
source: Rab5 was predominantly monoubiquitinated when FLAG-Rab5 was overexpressed with HA-ubiquitin in HEK 293T cells (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a demonstrating monoubiquitination bands in immunoblotting experiments.

claim: Monoubiquitinated Rab5 migrated in a gel as doublet bands, implying that monoubiquitination of Rab5 can occur at multiple sites.
source: Monoubiquitinated Rab5 migrated in a gel as doublet bands, implying that monoubiquitination of Rab5 can occur at multiple sites.
evidence: Observation of doublet bands in gel electrophoresis experiments provides direct experimental evidence.

claim: Appearance of doublet bands from monoubiquitination was previously noted for caveolin-1.
source: Appearance of doublet bands from monoubiquitination was previously noted for caveolin-1 (Ritz et al., 2011; Kirchner et al., 2013; Hayer et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies on caveolin-1.

claim: Double bands from the monoubiquitinated Rab5 remained unchanged in cells treated with GGTI-198, demonstrating that the double bands are the result of monoubiquitination of Rab5 at multiple sites.
source: Double bands from the monoubiquitinated Rab5 remained unchanged in cells treated with GGTI-198, demonstrating that the double bands are the result of monoubiquitination of Rab5 at multiple sites.
evidence: Experimental data from GGTI-198 treatment shown in Figure 1b demonstrates that prenylation is not responsible for doublet bands.

claim: The monoubiquitination of Rab5 is not dependent on the nucleotide binding state of Rab5.
source: Ubiquitination assays with GDP- and GTP-bound forms of Rab5 mutants (S34N and Q79L, respectively) revealed that the monoubiquitination of Rab5 is not dependent on the nucleotide binding state of Rab5 (Figure 1c).
evidence: Experimental data from ubiquitination assays with GDP- and GTP-bound mutants shown in Figure 1c.

claim: K140 is a major monoubiquitination site of Rab5.
source: We found that the upper band of the doublet was completely abolished in the K140R mutant, while the monoubiquitination bands of Rab5 were not altered in the other K-to-R mutants (Figure 1d). This result suggests that K140 is a major monoubiquitination site of Rab5, and that at least two or more sites are responsible for the lower band.
evidence: Experimental data from K-to-R mutant ubiquitination assays shown in Figure 1d.

claim: K33 and K134 form direct contacts with both GDP and GTP molecules.
source: Similarly, for Rab5, K33 and K134 form direct contacts with both GDP and GTP molecules (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b and c, PDB ID: 1TU4 and 3MJH, respectively).
evidence: Structural analysis based on crystal structures shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b and c.

claim: K33 and K134 are not responsible for monoubiquitination of Rab5.
source: No monoubiquitinated Rab5 band was detected for the 11KR mutant in the ubiquitination assay (Figure 1h), suggesting that K33 and K134 are not responsible for monoubiquitination of Rab5.
evidence: Experimental data from ubiquitination assay of 11KR mutant shown in Figure 1h.

claim: K116, K140, and K165 are monoubiquitination sites of Rab5.
source: Monoubiquitination bands were present for R116K, R140K, and R165K mutants in contrast to the 11KR mutant (Figure 1h). These results verified the previously known ubiquitination sites (K116 and K140) and revealed a novel ubiquitination site (K165).
evidence: Experimental data from R-to-K back-mutation ubiquitination assays shown in Figure 1h.

claim: K165 of Rab5 corresponds to K147 of a Ras GTPase whose monoubiquitination activates Ras signaling.
source: Interestingly, K165 corresponds to K147 of a Ras GTPase whose monoubiquitination activates Ras signaling (Baker et al., 2013a).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous study on Ras monoubiquitination.

claim: None of the three lysine residues (K116, K140, K165) are located in the Rab5 switch regions (SW I and SW II).
source: None of the three lysine residues are located in the Rab5 switch regions (SW I and SW II; Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: All of the lysine residues (K116, K140, K165) are surface-exposed and accessible to ubiquitin.
source: In addition, all of the lysine residues are surface-exposed and accessible to ubiquitin (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Upon transfection of ubiquitin into HeLa cells, endogenous Rab5-positive puncta diffused to the cytosol and failed to co-localize with early endosome antigen-1 (EEA1) protein.
source: Upon transfection of ubiquitin into HeLa cells, endogenous Rab5-positive puncta diffused to the cytosol and failed to co-localize with early endosome antigen-1 (EEA1) protein, another early endosome marker protein (Figure 2a).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Monoubiquitinated Rab5 was predominantly localized in the membrane fraction.
source: We observed that the monoubiquitinated Rab5 was predominantly localized in the membrane fraction.
evidence: Fractionation assay data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Monoubiquitinated Rab5 could disrupt Rab5-positive endosomal formation while it was localized on the membrane.
source: These results prompted us to hypothesize that monoubiquitinated Rab5 could disrupt Rab5-positive endosomal formation while it was localized on the membrane.
evidence: Hypothesis based on fractionation and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Ubiquitination of Rab5 has negative effects on the regulatory cycle of Rab5.
source: Together with the immunofluorescence assay results (Figure 2a–b), these findings strongly suggest that ubiquitination of Rab5 has negative effects on the regulatory cycle of Rab5.
evidence: Inference based on immunofluorescence and fractionation data.

claim: Overexpression of Rab5 apparently facilitated EGF-induced EGFR degradation, as judged by earlier complete degradation after 60 min of EGF treatment.
source: Overexpression of Rab5 apparently facilitated EGF-induced EGFR degradation, as judged by earlier complete degradation after 60 min of EGF treatment (Figure 2d upper-right panel).
evidence: EGFR degradation assay data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Overexpression of ubiquitin and Rab5 attenuated the degradation of EGFR, supported by the retention of some EGFR after 90 min of EGF treatment.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of ubiquitin and Rab5 attenuated the degradation of EGFR, supported by the retention of some EGFR after 90 min of EGF treatment (Figure 2d middle-left panel).
evidence: EGFR degradation assay data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: When the K140R mutant was overexpressed with ubiquitin EGFR degradation was completely restored and no attenuation was observed and almost all of the EGFR were degraded after 90 min of EGF treatment.
source: When the K140R mutant was overexpressed with ubiquitin EGFR degradation was completely restored and no attenuation was observed and almost all of the EGFR were degraded after 90 min of EGF treatment (Figure 2d lower-left panel), while the other mutants (K116R and K165R) still possesses such attenuation.
evidence: EGFR degradation assay data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Ubiquitination of K140 of Rab5 has a crucial role in downregulating the Rab5-mediated endocytic pathway.
source: This result suggests that ubiquitination of K140 of Rab5 has a crucial role in downregulating the Rab5-mediated endocytic pathway.
evidence: Inference based on EGFR degradation assay data.

claim: Rab5-positive endosomal puncta were abolished when Flag-Rab5 WT was co-transfected with HA-ubiquitin.
source: Consistent with the results obtained using endogenous Rab5 (Figure 2a–b), Rab5-positive endosomal puncta were abolished when Flag-Rab5 WT was co-transfected with HA-ubiquitin (Figure 2e,g).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2e,g.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K116 does not affect Rab5-positive endosomal formation.
source: Similarly, no puncta were observed for the K116R mutant upon co-transfection with HA-ubiquitin (Figure 2e,g), indicating that monoubiquitination of K116 does not affect Rab5-positive endosomal formation.
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2e,g.

claim: Rab5-positive endosomal puncta were detectable when either K140R or K165R mutants were co-transfected with HA-ubiquitin.
source: By contrast, Rab5-positive endosomal puncta were detectable when either K140R or K165R mutants were co-transfected with HA-ubiquitin (Figure 2e,g).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2e,g.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K140 or K165 inhibits the Rab5-positive endosomal formation.
source: These observations suggest that monoubiquitination of K140 or K165 inhibits the Rab5-positive endosomal formation.
evidence: Inference based on immunofluorescence data.

claim: No endosomal puncta were observed for either 11KR-R140K or 11KR-R165K mutants upon co-transfection with HA-ubiquitin.
source: However, no endosomal puncta were observed for either 11KR-R140K or 11KR-R165K mutants upon co-transfection with HA-ubiquitin (Figure 2f,h).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2f,h.

claim: Monoubiquitination of Rab5 on either K140 or K165 disrupts its function, whereas that of Ras on either K117 or K147 activates it.
source: These observations indicate that Rab5 monoubiquitination has functional consequences opposite those of Ras monoubiquitination (Baker et al., 2013a; Baker et al., 2013b): monoubiquitination of Rab5 on either K140 or K165 disrupts its function, whereas that of Ras on either K117 or K147 activates it.
evidence: Comparison with cited studies on Ras monoubiquitination.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K140 and K165 downregulates Rab5-mediated endocytic pathway, establishing monoubiquitination at specific sites of Rab5 as inhibitory signals, while monoubiquitination of K116 has no apparent effect.
source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that monoubiquitination of K140 and K165 downregulates Rab5-mediated endocytic pathway, establishing monoubiquitination at specific sites of Rab5 as inhibitory signals, while monoubiquitination of K116 has no apparent effect.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from multiple assays.

claim: The engineered Rab5 Del_Cys (C19S/C63S/Δ213–216) had the similar functionality as WT Rab5.
source: GEF assays confirmed that the engineered Rab5 Del_Cys (C19S/C63S/Δ213–216) had the similar functionality as WT Rab5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: GEF assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,b.

claim: Iterative addition of ubiquitinG76C resulted in 95% yield of monoubiquitinated Rab5 (mUbRab5).
source: Iterative additions of ubiquitin resulted in 95% yield of monoubiquitinated Rab5 (mUbRab5).
evidence: Experimental data from chemical ubiquitination procedure.

claim: All three mUbRab5s were monodisperse in solution (polydispersity <12%).
source: All three mUbRab5s were monodisperse in solution (polydispersity <12%; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Dynamic light scattering data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: All of the mUbRab5s were flexible in solution.
source: SAXS curves from the three mUbRab5s did not have a plateau in the Porod-Debye plot, implying that all of the mUbRab5s were flexible in solution (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: SAXS flexibility analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Distribution of conformational ensembles of mUbRab5K140 was clearly distinct from those of mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165.
source: Distribution of conformational ensembles of mUbRab5K140 was clearly distinct from those of mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165.
evidence: EOM analysis of SAXS data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Two distinct populations of conformational ensembles were evident for mUbRab5K140, with a radius-of-gyration (Rg) of 23 and 27 Å, respectively, and maximum distance (Dmax) of 75 and 90 Å.
source: Two distinct populations of conformational ensembles were evident for mUbRab5K140, with a radius-of-gyration (Rg) of 23 and 27 Å, respectively, and maximum distance (Dmax) of 75 and 90 Å (Figure 4b,e).
evidence: EOM analysis of SAXS data shown in Figure 4b,e.

claim: mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165 comprised a single population with an Rg of 25 Å and Dmax of 80 Å.
source: By contrast, mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165 comprised a single population with an Rg of 25 Å and Dmax of 80 Å (Figure 4a,d and and c,f).
evidence: EOM analysis of SAXS data shown in Figure 4a,d and c,f.

claim: Monoubiquitination at these three lysine sites has different functional consequences.
source: These results strongly suggest that monoubiquitination at these three lysine sites has different functional consequences.
evidence: Inference based on SAXS structural analysis.

claim: The ubiquitin moiety on K140 is more flexible than those on K116 and K165.
source: This indicates that the ubiquitin moiety on K140 is more flexible than those on K116 and K165.
evidence: Inference based on EOM structural models.

claim: None of the ubiquitin molecules from the EOM models were located proximal to Rab5.
source: Similar to the molecular dynamics simulation of mUbRas (Baker et al., 2013a), none of the ubiquitin molecules from the EOM models were located proximal to Rab5.
evidence: Structural analysis of EOM models.

claim: Monoubiquitination of Rab5 can regulate its function by altering its interactions with partner proteins such as GEF, GAP, and downstream effectors.
source: This raises the possibility that monoubiquitination of Rab5 can regulate its function by altering its interactions with partner proteins such as GEF, GAP, and downstream effectors.
evidence: Inference based on structural analysis.

claim: None of the ubiquitin moieties of mUbRab5s appeared to clash with Rabex-5.
source: In the mUbRab5:Rabex-5 complex models obtained by superpositioning of mUBRab5 and the Rab5:Rabex-5 structure (PDB ID: 4DQU) (Zhang et al., 2014), none of the ubiquitin moieties of mUbRab5s appeared to clash with Rabex-5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Structural modeling shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ubiquitin moieties might not interfere with activities related to a GEF, such as GDP release and GTP loading.
source: We speculated that the ubiquitin moieties might not interfere with activities related to a GEF, such as GDP release and GTP loading.
evidence: Speculation based on structural modeling.

claim: The ubiquitin moieties of mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165 were far from both Rabaptin5 and EEA1.
source: The ubiquitin moieties of mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165 were far from both Rabaptin5 and EEA1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Structural modeling shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The switch I (SWI) region of Rab5 was juxtaposed with the flexible ubiquitin moiety of mUbRab5K140.
source: However, the switch I (SWI) region of Rab5 was juxtaposed with the flexible ubiquitin moiety of mUbRab5K140, raising the possibility that a flexible ubiquitin moiety could cause a conformational change in the SWI.
evidence: Structural modeling and inference.

claim: Potential interruption of the SWI by mUbRab5K140 could have a severe impact on the Rab5 regulatory cycle.
source: Because this conformational change of SWI is required for activation of Rab5 through interactions with downstream effector proteins, potential interruption of the SWI by mUbRab5K140 could have a severe impact on the Rab5 regulatory cycle.
evidence: Inference based on structural modeling and known function of SWI.

claim: The ubiquitin moiety of mUbRab5K116 did not clash sterically with RabGAP-5.
source: The ubiquitin moiety of mUbRab5K116 did not clash sterically with RabGAP-5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4a).
evidence: Structural modeling shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4a.

claim: Both mUbRab5K140 and mUbRab5K165 seemingly bring the ubiquitin moieties close to RabGAP-5.
source: Both mUbRab5K140 and mUbRab5K165 seemingly bring the ubiquitin moieties close to RabGAP-5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4b,c), suggesting that neither mUbRab5K140 nor mUbRab5K165 would have enhanced interactions with RabGAP-5.
evidence: Structural modeling shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4b,c.

claim: The inhibitory effects of some mUbRab5s are highly likely to be caused by impedance of interactions with effector proteins.
source: Taken together, our structural analyses of mUbRab5s with partner proteins such as GEF, GAP, and effector proteins strongly suggest that the inhibitory effects of some mUbRab5s are highly likely to be caused by impedance of interactions with effector proteins.
evidence: Inference based on structural modeling of mUbRab5s with various partner proteins.

claim: Both mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K140 showed similar GDP-release activities to WT Rab5 in the presence of Rabex-5.
source: Both mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K140 showed similar GDP-release activities to WT Rab5 in the presence of Rabex-5, indicating that monoubiquitination of K116 and K140 does not interfere with the GEF function (Figure 5a,b).
evidence: GDP release assay data shown in Figure 5a,b.

claim: mUbRab5K165 exhibited reduced GDP release in the presence of GEF.
source: Notably, mUbRab5K165 exhibited reduced GDP release in the presence of GEF, and the curve could not be fitted by a one-phase decay linear regression model.
evidence: GDP release assay data shown in Figure 5a,b.

claim: mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K140 showed similar levels of GTP loading to Rab5.
source: Again, mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K140 showed similar levels of GTP loading to Rab5 (Figure 5c,d).
evidence: GTP loading assay data shown in Figure 5c,d.

claim: The fluorescence signal from mUbRab5K165 decreased continuously after it reached a maximum.
source: However, the fluorescence signal from mUbRab5K165 decreased continuously after it reached a maximum.
evidence: GTP loading assay data shown in Figure 5c,d.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K165 does not block GTP loading of Rab5, but can weaken the interaction between GTP and Rab5.
source: This observation indicates that monoubiquitination of K165 does not block GTP loading of Rab5, but can weaken the interaction between GTP and Rab5.
evidence: Inference based on GTP loading assay data.

claim: Monoubiquitination of Rab5 on K116 and K140 does not affect GEF activity, while monoubiquitination of K165 interferes with the GEF-mediated conversion cycle.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that monoubiquitination of Rab5 on K116 and K140 does not affect GEF activity, while monoubiquitination of K165 interferes with the GEF-mediated conversion cycle, as indicated by this protein's reduced response to GDP release and leakage during GTP loading.
evidence: Summary of GDP release and GTP loading assay data.

claim: The Kd value of mUbRab5K140 for Rabaptin5 was five-fold higher than that of unmodified Rab5 (37.7 ± 4.9 μM vs. 8.0 ± 3.4 μM).
source: Surprisingly, the Kd value of mUbRab5K140 for Rabaptin5 was five-fold higher than that of unmodified Rab5 (37.7 ± 4.9 μM vs. 8.0 ± 3.4 μM; Figure 6b,c and Table 4), indicating the reduced affinity of mUbRab5K140 for Rabaptin5.
evidence: Bio-layer interferometry data shown in Figure 6b,c and Table 4.

claim: mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165 showed little change in the Kd values for Rabaptin5: 8.0 ± 0.6 μM and 4.4 ± 0.2 μM, respectively.
source: However, mUbRab5K116 and mUbRab5K165 showed little change in the Kd values: 8.0 ± 0.6 μM and 4.4 ± 0.2 μM, respectively.
evidence: Bio-layer interferometry data shown in Figure 6b,c and Table 4.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K140 of Rab5 inhibits its binding to downstream effector proteins.
source: These results strongly suggest that monoubiquitination of K140 of Rab5 inhibits its binding to downstream effector proteins.
evidence: Inference based on bio-layer interferometry data.

claim: mUbRabK140 exhibited an approximately 20-fold increase in Kd for EEA1 compared to unmodified Rab5 (108.0 ± 22.0 μM vs. 5.8 ± 0.3 μM, respectively).
source: mUbRabK140 exhibited an approximately 20-fold increase in Kd for EEA1 compared to unmodified Rab5 (108.0 ± 22.0 μM vs. 5.8 ± 0.3 μM, respectively; Figure 6d,e and Table 4).
evidence: Bio-layer interferometry data shown in Figure 6d,e and Table 4.

claim: The Kd value of unmodified Rab5 for EEA1 was similar to that reported previously (5.8 ± 0.3 μM vs. 2.4 ± 0.23 μM).
source: The Kd value of unmodified Rab5 for EEA1 was similar to that reported previously (5.8 ± 0.3 μM vs. 2.4 ± 0.23 μM) (Mishra et al., 2010).
evidence: Comparison with cited previous study.

claim: mUbRab5K116 showed a modest increase in Kd value for EEA1 (18.4 ± 0.8 μM).
source: mUbRab5K116 showed a modest increase in Kd value for EEA1 (18.4 ± 0.8 μM), while mUbRab5K165 showed virtually no change (4.7 ± 0.5 μM) in Kd value relative to that of unmodified Rab5.
evidence: Bio-layer interferometry data shown in Figure 6d,e and Table 4.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K140 of Rab5 disrupts its interactions with down-stream effector proteins, while monoubiquitination of K116 only has a minor effect on these interactions.
source: Our results collectively establish that monoubiquitination of K140 of Rab5 disrupts its interactions with down-stream effector proteins, while monoubiquitination of K116 only has a minor effect on these interactions.
evidence: Summary of bio-layer interferometry data for both Rabaptin5 and EEA1.

claim: Monoubiquitination of Rab5 had an inhibitory effect on the regulatory cycle of Rab5.
source: In this study, we found that monoubiquitination of Rab5 had an inhibitory effect on the regulatory cycle of Rab5.
evidence: Summary of all experimental findings.

claim: Monoubiquitination seems to play different roles in Rab and Ras GTPases: monoubiquitination in Rab5 serves as an inhibitory signal, whereas it serves as a stimulatory or activating signal in Ras.
source: Therefore, monoubiquitination seems to play different roles in Rab and Ras GTPases: monoubiquitination in Rab5 serves as an inhibitory signal, whereas it serves as a stimulatory or activating signal in Ras.
evidence: Comparison with cited studies on Ras monoubiquitination.

claim: 28 of 63 human Rab GTPases (including isoforms) are ubiquitinated in cells.
source: Analysis of published proteomics data revealed that 28 of 63 human Rab GTPases (including isoforms) are ubiquitinated in cells.
evidence: Analysis of published proteomic data.

claim: K116 and K140 are located in non-conserved regions, while K165 is in the conserved G5 motif (xxxETSx'K').
source: When we compiled ubiquitination sites of Rab proteins reported by proteomic studies, we found that ubiquitination sites of Rab5 found in the current study - K116 and K140 - are located in non-conserved regions, while K165 is in the conserved G5 motif (xxxETSx'K') (Figure 8a).
evidence: Sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 8a.

claim: Both K116 and K165 are strictly conserved from yeast to human, whereas K140 is less conserved.
source: Analysis of Rab5 proteins from eukaryotic species revealed different degrees of conservation of the three ubiquitination sites discovered in this study: both K116 and K165 are strictly conserved from yeast to human, whereas K140 is less conserved (Figure 8b).
evidence: Sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 8b.

claim: K140 is replaced by isoleucine in Drosophila and glutamate in yeast.
source: K140 is replaced by isoleucine in Drosophila and glutamate in yeast, implying that K140 might be a point of functional differentiation in these organisms.
evidence: Sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 8b.

claim: The three ubiquitination sites were not conserved in Rab5 homologue from Acanthamoeba polyphaga mimivirus (APMV).
source: In contrast to eukaryotic Rab5 proteins, the three ubiquitination sites were not conserved in Rab5 homologue from Acanthamoeba polyphaga mimivirus (APMV).
evidence: Sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 8b.

claim: K165 of hRab5a is substituted to F152 in APMV Rab5 and plays a major role for binding to GTP molecule.
source: Recent crystal structure of APMV Rab5 revealed that K165 of hRab5a is substituted to F152 in APMV Rab5 and plays a major role for binding to GTP molecule (Ku et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited structural study of APMV Rab5.

claim: Monoubiquitination of Rab5 is a subsidiary signal for its regulation in eukaryotic cells.
source: Therefore, it seems that monoubiquitination of Rab5 is a subsidiary signal for its regulation in eukaryotic cells.
evidence: Inference based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: Ubiquitination of a conserved site can have different functional consequences in Rab and Ras GTPase proteins.
source: It is also intriguing that ubiquitination of a conserved site can have different functional consequences in Rab and Ras GTPase proteins.
evidence: Comparison of findings with cited Ras studies.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K165 of Rab5 has an inhibitory effect, whereas ubiquitination of the corresponding K147 of Ras has a stimulatory effect.
source: Monoubiquitination of K165 of Rab5 has an inhibitory effect, whereas ubiquitination of the corresponding K147 of Ras has a stimulatory effect (Baker et al., 2013a; Baker et al., 2013b).
evidence: Comparison with cited Ras studies.

claim: Monoubiquitination appears to be a versatile modification tool.
source: Therefore, monoubiquitination appears to be a versatile modification tool.
evidence: Inference based on comparison of Rab5 and Ras monoubiquitination effects.

claim: Oxidative conjugation of a ubiquitin moiety to a cysteine residue of a target protein has been widely used for chemical synthesis of ubiquitinated proteins.
source: Oxidative conjugation of a ubiquitin moiety to a cysteine residue of a target protein has been widely used for chemical synthesis of ubiquitinated proteins.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about chemical ubiquitination methods.

claim: Oxidative conjugation often suffers from incompleteness of the process, rendering subsequent separation of the ubiquitinated protein from unreacted protein very challenging.
source: Despite the relative simplicity of this method in comparison with enzymatic conjugation, oxidative conjugation often suffers from incompleteness of the process, rendering subsequent separation of the ubiquitinated protein from unreacted protein very challenging (Baker et al., 2013b; Merkley et al., 2005).
evidence: Cited previous studies on chemical ubiquitination methods.

claim: The optimized method for chemical synthesis of ubiquitinated proteins will facilitate studies on the effects of protein ubiquitination at the molecular level when no identified E3 ubiquitin ligase is available or a large quantity of ubiquitinated protein is desired.
source: Our optimized method for chemical synthesis of ubiquitinated proteins will facilitate studies on the effects of protein ubiquitination at the molecular level when no identified E3 ubiquitin ligase is available or a large quantity of ubiquitinated protein is desired.
evidence: Inference about the utility of the developed method.

claim: Only a small portion of Rab5 could be ubiquitinated when ubiquitin was overexpressed.
source: However, we did not find a stimulus signal or E3 ligase(s) responsible for monoubiquitination of Rab5. As result, only a small portion of Rab5 could be ubiquitinated when ubiquitin was overexpressed.
evidence: Observation from ubiquitination assays.

claim: Ubiquitination of Rab5 occurs rarely in cells under basal conditions.
source: These results suggest that ubiquitination of Rab5 occurs rarely in cells under basal conditions and may explain why the ubiquitination of Rab GTPases has not been studied until recently (de la Vega et al., 2011).
evidence: Inference based on experimental observations and cited literature.

claim: The effects of monoubiquitination of Rab5 were strong.
source: Despite the small population of monoubiquitinated Rab5, the effects of monoubiquitination of Rab5 were strong.
evidence: Summary of experimental observations.

claim: Monoubiquitination of Rab5 is tightly regulated in the cell through specific E3 ligase or DUB enzymes.
source: This suggests that monoubiquitination of Rab5 is tightly regulated in the cell through specific E3 ligase or DUB enzymes.
evidence: Inference based on the strong effects despite low abundance of monoubiquitinated Rab5.

claim: Rab GTPases regulate various vesicular trafficking processes such as endocytosis, exocytosis, and ER to Golgi transport.
source: Rab GTPases, the largest family of small GTPases, regulate various vesicular trafficking processes such as endocytosis, exocytosis, and ER to Golgi transport (Hutagalung and Novick, 2011).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Rab GTPases are activated by GTP binding and inactivated by the hydrolysis of GTP to GDP.
source: Rab GTPases are activated by GTP binding and inactivated by the hydrolysis of GTP to GDP (Pfeffer, 2005).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: A GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI) stabilizes GDP-bound Rab in the inactive state.
source: A GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI) stabilizes GDP-bound Rab in the inactive state.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about Rab GTPase regulation.

claim: A guanidine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) binds to GDP:Rab5 and catalyzes GDP release and GTP loading for Rab.
source: A guanidine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) binds to GDP:Rab5 and catalyzes GDP release and GTP loading for Rab.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about Rab GTPase regulation.

claim: The activated GTP-bound Rab exerts its effects by binding to various effector proteins.
source: The activated GTP-bound Rab exerts its effects by binding to various effector proteins.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about Rab GTPase regulation.

claim: Inactivation of GTP:Rab is aided by a GTPase activating protein (GAP).
source: Inactivation of GTP:Rab is aided by a GTPase activating protein (GAP) (Cherfils and Zeghouf, 2013), rendering the Rab GTPase ready for another cycle.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: K48-linked polyubiquitination guides the substrate to the proteasome, resulting in degradation of the substrate.
source: K48-linked polyubiquitination guides the substrate to the proteasome, resulting in degradation of the substrate (Komander and Rape, 2012; Hochstrasser, 2009; Akutsu et al., 2016).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: K63-linked polyubiquitination regulates cellular signaling pathways.
source: By contrast, K63-linked polyubiquitination regulates cellular signaling pathways (Bhoj and Chen, 2009).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Monoubiquitination modulates histone modification, virus budding, and endocytosis.
source: Monoubiquitination modulates histone modification, virus budding, and endocytosis (Hicke, 2001).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Site-specific monoubiquitination of K147 of Ras leads to activation of signaling by impairing its interaction with GAP.
source: Site-specific monoubiquitination of K147 of Ras leads to activation of signaling by impairing its interaction with GAP (Baker et al., 2013a; Baker et al., 2013b; Sasaki et al., 2011).
evidence: Cited previous studies on Ras monoubiquitination.

claim: Monoubiquitination of K117 of Ras facilitates GDP release from Ras, independent of a GEF.
source: In contrast, monoubiquitination of K117 of Ras facilitates GDP release from Ras, independent of a GEF (Baker et al., 2013b).
evidence: Cited previous study on Ras monoubiquitination.
